doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Quincy Jones's Body Heat
summary: Laws remembers Body Heat only vaguely. Brown praises its tracks and Bernard Ighner's Everything Must Change.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Oh. Is that the name of the record?
I can see the cover. It’s got the red light, a train coming.
Yeah. I remember that. I don’t remember the tunes so much, but I certainly remember that.

It’s got the Body Heat, Soul Saga (Song of the Buffalo Soldier), Everything Must Change, Boogie Joe the Grinder, One Track Mind, Just a Man, Along Came Betty – that’s the one that Bernard is killing – and then, for me, If I Ever Lose this Heaven. Oh man.

Yeah, for Everything Must Change, right. But, If I Ever Lose this Heaven, oh man. Al Jarreau doing all his vocal percussion. This one for, again, my generation, was another one of those that just looms large in our formation. Then back to Esther Phillips, Performance, CTI, small – oh, it’s got strings. Richard Tee, Pepper Adams, yourself.
